title: Finite morphisms are projective in the projective-bundle convention
statement: Let $h:T\to S$ be a finite morphism of schemes [def-weil-finite-integral-morphism]. Then $h$ is projective in the projective-bundle sense [def-trf-projective-bundle-morphism]: there is a quasi-coherent $\mathcal O_S$-module of finite type whose projective bundle contains $T$ as a closed subscheme over $S$.

source.place: Morphisms, Lemma 29.43.2 (Tag 0B3I), morphisms-lemma-finite-projective, together with Definition 29.43.1 (Tag 01W8), clause (1) (projective means a closed immersion into a projective bundle).

proof.text: Put $\mathcal E=h_*\mathcal O_T$ with its natural algebra structure. By [def-weil-finite-integral-morphism], $h$ is affine and $\mathcal E$ is quasi-coherent of finite type; over $V=\operatorname{Spec}R$ its inverse image is $\operatorname{Spec}A$ with $A$ finite over $R$.

source.place: Tag 0B3I (lemma-finite-projective), canonical embedding into P(h_*O_T); explicit graded-quotient verification by the worker

proof.text: Apply [lem-trf-positive-copy-graded-quotient] to $\mathcal E$. It supplies the quasi-coherent graded algebra $\mathcal B_0=\mathcal O_S$, $\mathcal B_n=\mathcal E$ for $n>0$, and the degree-preserving surjection $q:\operatorname{Sym}(\mathcal E)\twoheadrightarrow\mathcal B$. Both relative Proj schemes are defined [def-nagata-relative-proj]. The surjective-map clause of [prop-nagata-relative-proj-functoriality] gives a closed immersion $\iota:\operatorname{Proj}_S(\mathcal B)\hookrightarrow\mathbf P_S(\mathcal E)$, with the projective bundle as in [def-trf-projective-bundle-morphism].

source.place: Tag 0B3I (lemma-finite-projective), canonical embedding into P(h_*O_T); explicit graded-quotient verification by the worker

proof.text: Since $h$ is affine and $\mathcal E$ is quasi-coherent, [lem-trf-positive-copy-proj-affine-comparison] gives an $S$-isomorphism $\theta:\operatorname{Proj}_S(\mathcal B)\simeq T$. Compose $\theta^{-1}$ with $\iota$. This is a closed immersion: precomposition by an isomorphism preserves the homeomorphism onto a closed subset and the surjectivity of the structure-sheaf map [def-weil-closed-immersion]. It lies over $S$, and $\mathcal E$ is of finite type by Step 1, so [def-trf-projective-bundle-morphism] gives the required projectivity.
